Never Paste These
Student data — names, IDs, grades, attendance, anything from Skyward
Employee PII — SSNs, payroll, HR records, performance data
Credentials — passwords, API keys, tokens, login info for any system
When in doubt — don't paste it. See the Restricted Data Reference Guide or ask Adam.
The Three-Ingredient Formula — hit all three for a useful first draft
1 — What
The actual task
"Draft a response to this customer complaint." Not "I was wondering if maybe you could help me..."
2 — Context
The relevant situation
Paste the actual email, error message, or case note. The real thing beats a description of it every time.
3 — Format (optional)
What you want back
"Keep it under 3 sentences." "Formal — this is for a superintendent." "Use bullet points."
When the Response Isn't Right — Stay in the Conversation
Name what's wrong "Too formal — this customer is casual. Rewrite just the opening."
Add what you left out "Should have mentioned — this district is 3 months in, not new."
Keep what's working "First two paragraphs are good. Just rewrite the closing."
Ask for options "Give me two versions: one short and direct, one more detailed."
It's good at
Drafting emails, responses, and documents
Troubleshooting step by step
Explaining processes in plain language
Turning rough notes into polished writing
Keep in mind
Verify facts before using them
Doesn't remember previous conversations
Review output before sending — you're responsible for it
